ai.description: Vosmaer's Writhing Skink reaches 15 cm. It features a glossy, bronze-brown body with dark lateral stripes and a pale belly. Distinctive traits include a slender, elongated form and reduced limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Riopa vosmaerii* is best distinguished by its distinctively long, slender body and the presence of a single pair of enlarged nuchal scales behind the parietals.
ai.habitat: *Riopa vosmaerii* inhabits the leaf litter of moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: Vosmaeri's Writhing Skink is primarily crepuscular, emerging during twilight to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Riopa vosmaerii* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Riopa vosmaerii* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the dry deciduous forests and scrublands of Central and Peninsular India.
